tx_horror_movie_wall.blurb: Horror Movie Wall is one of the named cliffs inside the Monster Rock canyon, a limestone sport crag west of Austin. The face leans back slightly and stays shaded, which makes it a pleasant pick when the weather is warm. Eleven lines here, seven bolted for leading and four set up as top-ropes. The grades start near 5.9 and climb to the low 5.12s, but the heart of the wall is a run of 5.11s, so it suits climbers who already lead in the 5.10 range and want a progression. Some starts are short and begin from boulders. Routes carry film-themed names, in keeping with the rest of the canyon.

tx_motorboat_rock.blurb: Motorboat Rock is a big freestanding boulder that marks the entrance to Echo Canyon at Enchanted Rock State Natural Area, in the Texas Hill Country. Its eleven short routes mostly lean on traditional protection or top-rope, with a single bolted line, and they range from easy 5.6 terrain up to a stout 5.12. About half the grades sit in the 5.6 to 5.9 band, with a few harder 5.11 and 5.12 lines, and most lines can be reached from the top by scrambling up a gully, which is why guide services and first-time climbers gather here. The walk from the canyon floor is among the shortest in the park. Expect rope-draped faces and a crowd on nice weekends.

tx_orange_peel_area.blurb: Orange Peel Area is a wall of rust-colored granite tucked behind Motorboat Rock in Echo Canyon at Enchanted Rock. Most of the eleven lines here are traditional, with a pair of bolted ones, and the grade spread is wide: a handful of easy to moderate routes in the 5.6 to 5.9 range, a couple of 5.10s and 5.11s, and one route in the 5.13 range. One crack on the wall is considered among the best moderate trad lines in the park. The rock gives the area its name and makes the wall simple to spot. Echo Canyon can fill up on weekends, though there is usually something open to try.

tx_amazon_boulders.blurb: Amazon Boulders is a cluster of big granite blocks on the south side of Freshman Mountain, the smallest dome at Enchanted Rock State Natural Area. The eleven routes are a blend of bolted lines, gear-protected cracks and top-ropes, with short single-pitch climbing from moderate 5.7 and 5.8 up through a run of 5.11s and 5.12s and one 5.13. A well-liked crack on the 5.8 level suits trad climbers, while the sport lines run from 5.10 to the hard end. Freshman Mountain sees few climbers and hikers compared with the main dome, so the boulders tend to be quiet. Reaching them involves a slab scramble and a traverse around the south flank.

tx_main_canyon_left.blurb: Main Canyon Left is a long wall on the left side of the main canyon at Mineral Wells State Park in North Texas. The bluffs are about 20 to 40 feet tall, and nearly everything here is a top-rope climb, with one boulder problem added. Grades span from easy ground up to the low 5.11s; the middle of the wall holds the stiffer 5.9 and 5.10 lines, and the ends are gentler. Two crack lines are considered among the best in the park. The wall stays shaded most of the day and is still air, so it is best from late fall through spring. Many groups come simply to rappel the face.

tx_turkey_peak.blurb: Turkey Peak is a rugged granite summit beside the main dome at Enchanted Rock State Natural Area. Unlike the surrounding domes it is a true peak, and the climbing is concentrated high on its south-southwest face, where it feels exposed. Eleven routes mix trad, bolted and top-rope lines. Grades run from easy 5.4 and 5.5 ramps and scrambles through a cluster of 5.8s to a few 5.11s. The face is shaded early on summer mornings and catches warm, sheltered sun on winter afternoons. There is no official trail: expect a short steep scramble to the base and off-trail walking. The top rewards with views of the dome.
